Thanks Timothy — looping in Marissa (billing operations) and Logan (AP integrations).

Short answer: we can do either, but there are tradeoffs. For email PDFs we can:
- designate billing@redwoodinference.com as the invoice sender and append the PO number to the filename (we can automate filename formatting).
- provide a signed authorization form to confirm your AP team accepts invoices from that sender.

For portal/API push:
- It reduces manual steps and preserves structured invoice data (preferred for high-volume customers).
- Onboarding takes 2–4 weeks for certificate exchange and testing, but we can scope a light-weight push for month-to-month if you want to pilot.

Marissa — can you confirm the exact fields we need on the invoice (PO on file name, remittance details) and whether we can auto-name the PDF to include the PO? Logan — can you outline the minimal steps for an API test (if NobleApps wants to pilot).

Best,

Hi Timothy —

We can absolutely do the email-PDF route with the PO in the filename. Requirements and notes:
- Required invoice fields: invoice number, invoice date, total, VAT breakdown (if applicable), our remittance instructions (bank details), and a visible PO number on both PDF body and file name.
- Filename format we can emit: Redwood_Invoice_<INVNUM>_PO<PO#>.pdf (we'll replace slashes with dashes).
- Signed "invoice sender authorization" (attached) is preferred for your audit; please sign and return so your AP system accepts our email sender as canonical.
- Exceptions: if your AP system enforces an EDI/Peppol/UBL intake, the portal/API path is necessary. Otherwise email PDFs are fine as long as the PO validator can pick up the file name.

Attached: signed-invoice-authority-form.pdf (fill signature, company stamp)

If you want to pilot API push, Logan can propose a minimal exchange (TLS cert + test payload) and we can schedule a 30-minute run-through. Otherwise we'll set billing@redwoodinference.com as the canonical sender and start the automated file-naming next invoice cycle.

Cheers,
